subject: Texas AI Docket, Carousel No. 28, September 18th, 2026, Who writes the record
body:
Who writes the record

Carousel No. 28, September 18th, 2026

Shipped under target at 6.8 against 8.0

claimsPASS, 18 verified claim(s)
renderPASS, 9 slide(s)
qaPASS, 9 slide(s), zero fails, zero warns
aggregatesPASS, 7 declaration(s), 9 numeric phrase(s) in the render, all re-derived
assemblyPASS, 9 slide(s), 14.81 MB, vector
scoreWARN, 6.8 against 8.0 target; 6 rounds, cap 5; not a ship failure
labelsPASS, 54 claim id(s) checked, every label beside one traces to the shape its claim proves
quantifiersPASS, 86 published string(s) read from one list, every universal names its set
verbatimPASS, 15 declared fragment(s) over 9 of 9 dossier(s), every one a literal substring of its own claim's quote, 1 slot note(s)
dossiersPASS, 39,231 chars planned
captionPASS, 131 words
craft floorPASS, 9 frame(s), median 2457, floor 442
plan vs renderWARN, 14 of 52 acceptance item(s) checkable
texanWARN, places Hays County, Tyler / body yes / deadline yes / next step NO
absencesPASS, 9 of 9 scoped to a named document
numeralsPASS, 12 numeral(s) over 9 frame(s), every one reachable
completionPASS, the deck shipped
constructionADVISORY, 6 of 9 bright-region boxes; two are false object matches; bespoke check and panel remain authoritative

What degraded

  • The record shipped 4 admitted items rather than 5. A code review found that one of them duplicated an item already on main, and it was removed after its new quotes were folded into the original.
  • The Supabase connector is enabledInChat: false, so the Bottleneck Scanner daily-cap query could not run. Reported rather than silently skipped.
  • faa.gov returned 403 on four attempts for the Zipline environmental assessment, the fourth consecutive run with a 403 from this host. The story was dropped rather than sourced to journalism about a document nobody here read.
  • The deck scored 6.8 against the 8.0 quality target with zero hard failures. It completed the bounded search after six rounds and ships with the shortfall named.
  • Frames 3, 5 and 7 were named by all three judges across three rounds as the only frames whose largest shape is a flat fill, and were NOT redrawn. Three earlier art repairs in this run each introduced a defect the next round caught, and the final scoring round has no reviewer after it. Both judges were told that reasoning and both said it was right.
  • construction_check reported six bright bounding boxes, but frames 1 and 3 are a lit records-room wall and a car scene, not document plates. The pixel measurement is retained as an advisory; bespoke_check and the scoring panel remain the release gates for genuinely repeated artwork.

Named here rather than left out. A run that quietly ships less than it planned teaches nobody anything.

Post this

Upload the PDF to LinkedIn as a document, title it Who writes the record, paste the post copy under it, then paste the first comment within a minute of posting.

carousel.pdf   contact sheet   the site

1. The post copy

One agenda line carries the sheriff's no.

The September 1st Hays County Commissioners Court agenda carried an item acknowledging the Sheriff's Office commitment "to not activate or implement Axon Draft One", an "AI-enabled report-writing feature".

September 8th put the "governance of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in connection with surveillance equipment" in front of the same court for "possible adoption of a policy statement".

On September 15th the County Clerk's Office asked to obtain AI Minutes through Govably "in the amount of $19,200.00 for year one" and to waive the purchasing policy of obtaining three quotes.

The county's minutes archive stops at July 28th. No outcome for any of them is published there. How much of what those meetings did is anywhere a Hays County resident can read?

#HaysCounty #AxonDraftOne #Govably

2. The first comment

The machine changed itself

  • `noun_trace` can go red. The report line states its advisory contract, and the two states in which the scan measures nothing at all, a gazetteer that loaded no place and claims carrying no text, are hard fails.
    The fails list was `[]` written as a literal, so no input in this gate's history could have produced exit 1. The 2026-09-18 run cited its exit 0 as evidence four times and it was evidence of nothing. `gate_wiring.py` exists for a checker connected to nothing and could not see this one, because this gate IS wired, IS invoked and DOES run: what was empty is the only channel by which running could change an outcome. A round-3 judge found it by reading the source.
  • `absence_check` no longer accepts the absent document as its own scope. A doc word is disqualified when the sentence's negation attaches to it as its subject, and a locator preposition governing it settles the case first.
    Frame 9 shipped "The minutes that would record an outcome are not published." into round 3 and this gate passed it. Frame 8, one swipe earlier, carries the correct scope. The gate's own docstring already warned about this for the INDEFINITE case, 'the absent thing, not the source', so the article was never what separated a source from a missing thing. The test was for a noun shape and the defect was a missing scope.
  • `layout_check --prose` discovers its surfaces instead of listing them, and the three stale statements that discovery found were fixed.
    The list was six paths and `knowledge/carousel/SLIDE_DOSSIER_SPEC.md` was not one of them, so the surface the dossier phase reads stated 'no repeat in a row, at least five distinct' for nine days after the 2026-09-16 rebalance, with that exact phrase already in the gate's own SUPERSEDED_PHRASES. GATE_LESSONS 39: when a gate selects what to examine the default must be EXAMINE with named exemptions, because an allowlist fails silent and nothing reports the omission.

Every change is logged in ledger/carousel/upgrades.json.

Notes

A CODE REVIEW ON THE PULL REQUEST CAUGHT A DUPLICATE IN THE RECORD AND TWO CLAIM GAPS, and all three are fixed. tx-2026-0167 was the UT San Antonio flood sensor already published as tx-2026-0141, off the same article reached over http rather than https. Its two genuinely new quotes were folded into the existing item and the duplicate was removed before it reached main, so the record is 145 items rather than 146. The admission phase did not see it because the dedupe compares entities and keywords and does not normalise source URLs. The other two are the deck's own defect family in the record: tx-2026-0147 stated the El Paso items as filed as though they were what the council enacted, with the approved-as-revised fact arriving fifth, and tx-2026-0166 published a recruitment status, a sponsor role and two dates with no claim behind any of them. The registry was re-fetched and four claims added, and that item's reader-facing link pointed at a JSON API rather than the human study page a prospective participant would follow. THE RECORD CAUGHT TWO MOVEMENTS A STRING TEST WOULD HAVE MISSED. El Paso's council voted on the plate reader item while its agenda text stayed byte for byte identical, so a diff would have returned 'no change' and been wrong; the Legistar meeting detail carried Approved as Revised on both items. PGRR144 reached a board vote recommending approval, caught by reading the board material rather than the item page. THE DECK TOOK SEVEN SCORING ROUNDS AND PRODUCED FIVE HARD FAILS, AND NOT ONE WAS IN A QUOTE, A NUMERAL OR A CLAIM. The claims file was exact in every round. All five were ordinary declarative sentences between the quotes: a universal about how often this court posts an agenda, an assertion about who publishes those agendas, a role read off bold type, and a pronoun with three antecedents. Two were created by the previous round's own repair. Four were sentences added to give a reader something the run had not fetched, so the last one was DELETED rather than rewritten, and the gap is named in the run record instead. THE SAME UNSOURCED ASSERTION HAD ALSO REACHED THE PUBLIC RECORD, in tx-2026-0168's public_access field, which read that this court 'meets in public and posts its agendas in advance'. No fetched page states it. It is gone from there too. THREE GATES IN THIS REPO CANNOT FAIL AND THIS RUN FOUND ALL THREE. noun_trace returns a hardcoded empty fails list, so its exit 0 has never meant anything. The render harness collects window.__akLeaders, a prefix left behind by a port, while these frames set window.__txLeaders. And it is not only leaders: rules, contacts, encodings, svg_plates and canvas_text are empty on all nine slides of every deck this repo has shipped, so the declarative half of every acceptance list has never been machine checked. A qa.py PASS certifies something narrower than it looks like. THE BIGGEST SINGLE MISS, and it is a research one. One fetch of the Hays County Commissioners Court's own landing page would have returned the meeting day, the hour, the address and the members' precincts. Every scoring round asked the deck for something a reader could do, three answers were written to fill that hole and two hard-failed for being unsourced, and the run had already reached that domain for the minutes archive without ever asking for the body's own page. NOTHING PROMPTED. prompt_audit measured 1455 tool calls and none waited on a human. That is the Phase 19 reading rather than the interim one, which stood at 1,252.

This is a draft. Nothing was sent. The deck is already merged to main, so these links are live. Posting is the only step left, and it is yours.
